27613.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience the fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team.
We are currently looking for a suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the
Grants Compliance Manager
to be based in
Port Moresby
,
Papua New Guinea.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
To lead, manage, and provide strategic direction for the grant compliance framework of the Global Fund portfolio. This role ensures robust internal controls, manages high-level donor audits, and oversees all sub-grantee compliance. The Manager also leverages this portfolio expertise to develop standardized compliance resources and provide expert technical support.
MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Strategic Compliance Leadership & Management
A robust, proactive, and efficient compliance system is established, minimizing risk and ensuring adherence to all donor/legal standards.
Design, implement, and lead the grant's overall internal control framework to prevent and detect fraud and mismanagement.
Lead and manage all high-level donor inquiries, external audits, and investigations, serving as the primary focal point.
Oversee the comprehensive risk management process, ensuring the risk register is current and mitigation plans are effective.
Advise Senior Leadership (DCOP, COP) on all compliance matters, providing solutions-oriented recommendations.
Manage and mentor the compliance team (implied), setting performance goals and fostering professional development.
Sub-Grantee Oversight & Partnership
.
Sub-grantees have the capacity and systems to be compliant, and grant objectives are achieved through effective partnership.
Lead the strategic oversight of the entire sub-grantee management lifecycle, from due diligence to close-out.
Lead high-level negotiations on sub-award agreements, amendments, and budget realignments.
Design and direct the portfolio's sub-grantee capacity-building strategy, ensuring training is targeted and effective.
Ensure all sub-grantee financial and programmatic reporting is reviewed, consolidated, and validated.
Technical Support & Resource Development
WV offices in the region have enhanced capacity to manage Global Fund grants, and compliance tools are standardized and effective.
Author, develop, and standardize key compliance resources, including manuals, handbooks, and training modules for the portfolio.
Provide expert technical assistance (remote and in-person) to other WV offices in the region with Global Fund grants –
if required
.
Design and facilitate regional capacity-building workshops and trainings on Global Fund compliance
High-Level Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement
Donors and stakeholders are confident in WV PNG's management of the grant, and all reporting is timely and accurate.
Ensure all financial reports for the Global Fund are consolidated, accurate, and submitted on time.
Represent World Vision PNG in high-level meetings and negotiations with donors, government partners, and sub-grantees.
Ensure timely and accurate reporting of progress and compliance to all stakeholders
Major responsibilities – National Office Support
Coordinates the designing and implementing of overall risk management process for the organization, which includes leading the Enterprise Risk Management in WV PNG by mobilizing and ensuring that the Risk Management Committee is functional
Leads the monitoring, updating, and cascading of strategic (High Level) Risk Register and provides recommendations related to risk for Leadership decision-making
Coordinates changes to Risk Management Framework and Risk Registry
Acts as the point person of WVPNG for Regional and Partnership Risk Management engagements
Performs risk assessment – analysing current risks and identifying potential risks that are affecting the organization and risk evaluation
Recommends risk responses including reactive messaging or communication and monitor on management’s behalf
Monitor the progress of risk mitigation activities, updates and manages WVPNG’s Risk Appetite ensuring alignment with the Partnership
Coordinates with directors and department risk owners in making sure that department risk registers are in place and monitored
Safeguarding
Audits
Compliance training
Ensures that the operations and business transactions of WV PNG follow all relevant legal and internal rules
Advises management on best practices for compliance, input on business decisions and contract negotiations to ensure organization’s compliance with laws and regulations through detailed report
Works closely with all the department to ensure that all actions of the organization and its contractors and other engagements operate within all regulatory guidance, statutory and legislative requirements
Conducts overall monitoring of compliance of WV PNG’s Standard of Procedure and Partnership and National Office policies
Provides support to the different teams during internal and external audit and ensures that audit recommendations are implemented and complied with
Support to GAM with due diligence screening for compliance partnership of private sectors or CSO that WVPNG intends to work
Carries out all other duties as may be reasonably assigned from time to time, within the level of the job
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum 3-5 years’ experience in grant compliance, finance, or audit.
At least 3 years in a management or leadership position.
Demonstrated expert knowledge of Global Fund rules and regulations.
Proven experience in developing training materials, manuals, and policies.
Experience managing complex sub-grantee portfolios.
Familiar with risk management and industry standards
Strong interpersonal skills, along with the ability to communicate effectively with others at all levels of the organization
Knowledge of legal requirements and controls
Familiarity with industry practices and professional standards
Experience providing regional or multi-country technical support.
Strong leadership, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.
Demonstrated ability to design and implement new systems and policies.
Knowledge in ISO 31000 Risk Management is an advantage
Based in Port Moresby with required travel to project sites and potentially to other countries in the region for technical support
Fluency in English (written and verbal) and Tok Pisin
Be available to work on weekends and on short notice.
Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in one PDF file before;
16 July 2026, 12:00 AM UTC
Expression of interest
Detailed CV
Valid Police & Medical Clearance Certificate
World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
World Vision is committed to the protection of children. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our child protection practices. Hence employment is conditional upon successful completion of all applicable background checks, including criminal record checks, where possible.
We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within
two (2) weeks
of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.

27589.description:
Family Health International (FHI360) is a global development organization with a rigorous, evidence-based approach. Our professional staff includes experts in health, nutrition, education, economic development civil society, environment, and research. FHI 360 operates from 60 offices with 4,400 staff in the U.S. and around the world. Our commitment to partnerships at every level and our multidisciplinary approach enable us to have a lasting impact on the individuals, communities, and countries we serve–improving lives for millions.
Meeting Targets and Maintaining Epidemic Control (EpiC), a global project funded by the
U.S. Department of State (US DoS), provides strategic technical assistance and direct service delivery to achieve HIV epidemic control Among at-risk and vulnerable populations and strengthen global health security, including COVID-19 response.
EpiC is led by FHI 360 with core partners Right to Care (RTC), Palladium, and Population Services International (PSI). Starting in early 2020, EpiC responded to the global COVID-19 pandemic by supporting partner governments to prevent, prepare for, and respond to COVID-19 and bolster health systems.
FHI 360, in collaboration with the National Department of Health (NDoH) plans to create a costed medical oxygen roadmap for Papua New Guinea (PNG), through strengthened medical oxygen systems across the country by improving access, utilization, and management of oxygen-related equipment in public health facilities. One key outcome of this process is the creation of a National Medical Oxygen Policy to guide the planning, regulation, financing, and sustainable use of medical oxygen services across the country.
FHI 360 in collaboration with the NDoH have developed a draft Medical Oxygen Policy through technical consultations and stakeholder engagement. To progress this draft to formal vetting within NDoH and ultimately to approval by the National Executive Council (NEC), FHI 360 is seeking to contract a short-term consultant specialised in technical and policy support, to collaborate with the NDoH Policy Unit to progress this work. As part of this effort, FHI 360 seeks to engage a Local Policy Development Expert. FHI360, is therefore, seeking qualified candidates for the following role:
Short Term Consultant Local Policy Development Expert
RESPONSIBILITIES
Reviewed and refined draft National Medical Oxygen Policy (final version ready for NDoH vetting).

Proven experience in health policy development and PNG government policy processes.

27261.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our APD team, you will work coordinate a team of APD officers to ensure the safety of our growing gold site in the Eastern Highlands. In this role you will assist with the development of operational security systems, develop standard operating procedures, and provide training in security emergency related preparedness
Key Accountabilities
Proactively engage with the APD Supervisors to provide security advice and support to the APD Teams to ensure APD fleet availability and security targets are achieved and optimised against budget.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for security /or support within the mine site area, underground or in the field as required to ensure security on equipment and people`s life is minimised.
Perform troubleshooting to identify and remedy issues that may arise.
Support and assist the APD team to ensure the rectification of identified defect equipment to improve and optimise availability and reliability targets.
Work closely with the Superintendent APD to assess performance and identify improvement projects to maximise results, reduce risk and implement cost management initiatives.
Maintain the Gold Room security system and ensure that the contract between the owners and contractors relating to the movement of gold, is carried out in accordance with K92 Mining Limited`s procedures.
Establish a high-performance culture by motivating team members to achieve a high level of performance and by rewarding and recognising high performance.
Appraise and evaluate direct reports in accordance with K92 Mining Limited ’s Work Performance systems   process by providing individual performance feedback, giving guidance and direction, and developing and agreeing on improvement plans
Ensure effective processes for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members are in place.
Direct and train employees on the APD process, procedure, and Equipment.
Continuously mentor and coach technicians on effective repair techniques.
Identify skills gaps and training requirements and assist in developing training packages as required to close the skills gap.
Actively review the work performance of APD Supervisors and provide feedback to the APD Superintendent including the talent and succession planning for designated key roles.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will require a minimum level of Grade 10 education and a minimum of 5 years’ experience in mining and fire & emergency response disciplines.
Successful completion of accredited safety, fire, and emergency response training.
Competent in breathing apparatus, rescue from height, confined space rescue and fire response.
Experience in fire suppression equipment maintenance.
Current Occupational First Aid Certificate.
Good written and oral communication skills in English and Pidgin.
Ability to write reports and have good computer skills in Word & Excel.
Proven man management and supervisory skills.
Good, demonstrated skills in Radio / telephone procedures.
Sound incident investigation skills.
Truck driving license.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

JOB DESCRIPTION
To assist the Principal Financial Analyst (Strategy and Risk Management) in the analysis, management and reporting of the financial risks of the Government's debt portfolio and to assist in the formulation of relevant strategies and policies to manage financial risks related to Government debt, provide technical and policy advice and support to government and other agencies on management of these risks
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES
To assist the Principal Financial Analyst, and provide leadership to junior staff, to derive polices, strategies, and plans, formulate legislation and provide technical and policy advice to other agencies in executing the priorities of the Branch which includes:
Ensure financial risk is minimized by using analysis to keep within the parameters of the Medium-Term Debt Strategy.
Ensure appropriate analysis and reporting is provided to management and others on different financing and loan proposals.

Contribute to operation of the Division and the Branch, in accordance with the Treasury strategic plan, and Divisional and Branch work plans

27686.description:
Economist - Fiscal & Monetary Policy, Grade 13
JOB DESCRIPTION
To assist and support the Senior Economist and the Principal Economist - Fiscal and Monetary Policy in developing macroeconomic policies in relation to the fiscal and monetary policies, and in coordinating and monitoring the implementation of these policies and its interaction with the monetary policy.
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES
Assist and support the Senior Economist and the Principal Economist - Fiscal and Monetary Policy to formulate fiscal policy and assess its impact on the operations of the monetary policy to realise the priorities and work plans for the branch:
Develop and advise on the Governments macroeconomic policies including fiscal and monetary policy.
Provide input to the annual budget and coordinate preparation of relevant documentation (Volume 2 of the Economic Policy Document of the budget and appropriate legislative amendments, briefs and submissions for both Parliament and Cabinet).
Coordinate and monitor the implementation of the Governments macroeconomic policies in relation to expenditure and revenue and financing through publication of Fiscal Outtum Reports and Monthly Warrant Ceiling.
Meet international standards for reporting on fiscal policy.
Monitor and assess the interaction of Governments fiscal policy with monetary policy (i.e, nature, composition and magnitude of public debt, expenditure and revenue having impact on the monetary policy variables).
Review and advise on the broad components of Government expenditure (recurrent, development, salaries and wages and externally financed versus domestic financing).
Promote and encourage dialogue with Government departments, statutory bodies and relevant stakeholders to monitor and tract Government expenditures to ensure that there are no wastage of public funds and value for its expenditure is derived.
MAJOR DUTIE
With assistance from and as directed by the Assistant Secretary or the Principal Economist, assess and analyse fiscal policy issues and its impact on the operations of the monetary policy.
Consolidate and analyse fiscal data on a monthly, six-monthly and annual basis and advise Secretary and Minister on the implementation of the budget.
Provide advice to Secretary and Minister on the performance of revenue by monitoring weekly and monthly cash flow situations and Budget implementation on a regular basis.
Provide advice on the overall level of Government expenditure, revenue and public sector borrowing requirements. These responsibilities include reviews of broad components of Government expenditures and intra-public sector fiscal arrangements.
Monitor the implications of Governments fiscal policy on monetary policy.
Represent the Branch and the Division on relevant inter-departmental committees such as Public Debt Committee (PDC), Authority to Pre-Commit Committee (APC), etc.
JOB REQUIREMENTS
QUALIFICATIONS & ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Essential
Qualifications:
Bachelor Degree in Economics, Finance, or Public Policy Management from a recognised university or a learning institution.
Work experience:
Prior relevant work experience on Economics, Finance, or Public Policy Management role.
Teamwork:
Able to work well with colleagues, respond to requests in a timely manner and share relevant information with the Division, the Department and with other stakeholders. Contribute to identifying any team development needs and building the capacity and capability of the team.
Workload and time management:
Contribute to identifying team priorities, and share or allocate specific tasks within team and to ensure competing deadlines are met. Manage own tasks within this environment. Promote effective and efficient service delivery.
Strategic and budget planning skills:
Contribute, as required, to identifying divisional and department strategic goals and budget plans and assist in the preparation of related documentation to support the meeting of these strategic goals and budget plans, as necessary.
Financial management:
Ensure all expenditure, acquittals and other financial and commercial transactions strictly adhere to Departmental and Government-wide policies and/or legislation.
Legislative knowledge:
Establish knowledge about the range of Acts, laws and policies governing the work of this role and the Department of Treasury more broadly.
Values:
Demonstrate and practice high levels of integrity, honesty, accountability, respect and wisdom and accept responsibility for one's own actions at all times.
Zero tolerance of any unethical activity or behaviour:
Must be a positive role model on ethical behaviour for staff and demonstrate personal qualities of honesty, fairness and professionalism.
Computing:
Demonstrate proficiency in the use of email and internet, in the application of software such as MS Word and MS Excel to perform tasks, and in the creation of presentations using MS PowerPoint.
Technical:
A demonstrated knowledge/understanding of fiscal policy in relation to expenditure, revenue and financing.
Desirable
Work experience:
Substantial experience at an equivalent level of employment with similar levels of responsibility.

27262.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our APD team, you will work coordinate a team of APD officers to ensure the safety of our growing gold site in the Eastern Highlands. In this role you will assist with the development of operational security systems, develop standard operating procedures, and provide training in security emergency related preparedness
Key Accountabilities
Proactively engage with the APD Supervisors to provide security advice and support to the APD Teams to ensure APD fleet availability and security targets are achieved and optimised against budget.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for security /or support within the mine site area, underground or in the field as required to ensure security on equipment and people`s life is minimised.
Perform troubleshooting to identify and remedy issues that may arise.
Support and assist the APD team to ensure the rectification of identified defect equipment to improve and optimise availability and reliability targets.
Work closely with the Superintendent APD to assess performance and identify improvement projects to maximise results, reduce risk and implement cost management initiatives.
Maintain the Gold Room security system and ensure that the contract between the owners and contractors relating to the movement of gold, is carried out in accordance with K92 Mining Limited`s procedures.
Establish a high-performance culture by motivating team members to achieve a high level of performance and by rewarding and recognising high performance.
Appraise and evaluate direct reports in accordance with K92 Mining Limited ’s Work Performance systems   process by providing individual performance feedback, giving guidance and direction, and developing and agreeing on improvement plans
Ensure effective processes for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members are in place.
Direct and train employees on the APD process, procedure, and Equipment.
Continuously mentor and coach technicians on effective repair techniques.
Identify skills gaps and training requirements and assist in developing training packages as required to close the skills gap.
Actively review the work performance of APD Supervisors and provide feedback to the APD Superintendent including the talent and succession planning for designated key roles.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will require a minimum level of Grade 10 education and a minimum of 5 years’ experience in mining and fire & emergency response disciplines.
Successful completion of accredited safety, fire, and emergency response training.
Competent in breathing apparatus, rescue from height, confined space rescue and fire response.
Experience in fire suppression equipment maintenance.
Current Occupational First Aid Certificate.
Good written and oral communication skills in English and Pidgin.
Ability to write reports and have good computer skills in Word & Excel.
Proven man management and supervisory skills.
Good, demonstrated skills in Radio / telephone procedures.
Sound incident investigation skills.
Truck driving license.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

27596.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life. Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
Area Programme Manager
to be based in
Arawa, Autonomous Region of Bouganive.
The Area Program Manager will provide leadership, management and overall supervision of all project activities implemented within the Arawa Area Programme to ensure World Vision Papua New Guinea’s strategic objectives and child wellbeing outcomes are achieved.
The role is responsible for leading the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of programs within the Arawa region, ensuring activities are delivered within scope, time, budget and quality standards. The Area Program Manager will provide day-to-day operational leadership, manage Area Programme budgets and resources, support grant management, ensure compliance with financial and organisational standards, and respond to audit findings and risks.
The position will work closely with Portfolio Managers, Project Supervisors, government authorities, community leaders, donors, partners and other stakeholders to ensure programs are responsive to local needs and aligned with organisational priorities. The role will also contribute to project design, proposal development, community needs identification, policy engagement, advocacy and partnership building at Area Programme, district and provincial levels.
The Area Program Manager will provide people-centred leadership to staff within the Area Programme, supporting coaching, mentoring, performance management, learning, succession planning, employee relations, safeguarding, security and staff wellbeing. The role will also support programme effectiveness and quality assurance through baseline activities, monitoring, evaluation, research, learning, child participation and appropriate case management processes that protect and promote the wellbeing of children.
Educational Qualification/Skills, Knowledge & Experience
Experience in program management within a complex international organisation, preferably in an NGO context.
Knowledge and understanding of World Vision operations will be an added advantage.
Experience in project design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and report writing.
Computer literacy in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
A minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field.
A Master’s degree in a related field will be an added advantage.
Relevant training or certification in program management, particularly within an NGO context.
At least five years of relevant experience, preferably in program management within an NGO or development context.
Strong leadership and project management skills.
Excellent negotiation and decision-making skills.
Strong analytical, interpersonal and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work with minimum supervision in a cross-cultural environment.
Ability to work under pressure and meet strict deadlines while maintaining a positive attitude.
Demonstrated financial management skills.
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.
Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in one PDF file before;
Tuesday 14th July, 2026, (Midnight, PNG Time)
Expression of interest
Detailed CV
World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children and adults living where World Vision operates. We enforce a zero tolerance policy for any forms of violence, abuse and exploitation against children or adults, either by employees or others affiliated with our work. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our safe guarding practices. Employment is conditional upon successful completion of all mandatory background checks, including criminal record checks, where required.
We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within
two (2) weeks
of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.
Applicant Types Accepted:
Local Applicants Only.
Apply now and take the next step in your carrer with this amazing opportunity!
Apply

27564.description:
Work with an organisation built on Christian Values
Serve with purpose - supporting aviation that brings help and hope across PNG
Oversees transactional finance operations
The Company
A well-established, international aviation organisation with a strong Christian foundation, providing life-saving transport and support to remote communities across Papua New Guinea. Operating light aircraft and other essential technologies, the team connects isolated populations with healthcare, education, and development services. Rooted in faith and committed to safety, reliability and service, the organisation blends professional aviation standards with deep community impact
About the role
We are seeking an experienced Transactional Finance Manager based in Mt Hagen to oversee transactional finance operations and support the Head of Finance in safeguarding the programme’s financial integrity. You will lead the transactional accounts team, ensure accurate financial reporting, and strengthen internal controls across all accounting processes.
Key Responsibilities
Support the PNG Head of Finance in financial management, including preparation of annual financial plans, ad-hoc reports, and credit control activities
Oversee month-end and year-end processes, including financial reporting, reforecasts, reconciliations, and liaison with external auditors
Assist in the completion of company statistical returns including the preparation and payment of GST and Withholding Tax (WHT) to ensure timely submission and payment.
Oversee day-to-day transactional finance operations including accounts Payable, accounts receivable, and income processing
Lead and manage the Transactional Finance Team, including performance monitoring, training, coaching, and system/process improvements (e.g. NetSuite)
Strengthen internal controls and ensure compliance with policies and statutory requirements
Lead and develop the transactional finance team, including coaching and performance management
Qualifications, Skills & Experience
CPA qualifications with a tertiary qualification in accounting or related field (desirable)
Minimum 3 years’ accounting experience, including 2–3 years in a supervisory or team leadership role
Strong understanding of transactional accounting processes and financial controls
Strong attention to detail, organisation and communication skills
To apply for this position, interested candidates are asked to submit:
A cover letter addressing key criteria of the role
An updated CV in Microsoft Word format, outlining employment history, educational qualifications, and listing three referees (referees will only be contacted if shortlisted)
Our client's priority is to provide opportunities to high performing Papua New Guineans for this position.  Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

27493.description:
REnew Pacific Project Manager
Position Description
Reporting to:
Program Operations Director
Work location:
Autonomous Region of Bougainville
Department:
Program Operations
Budget holder:
Yes, as delegated under the IDD
Grade
G6
Direct reports:
1
Here you’ll make a difference
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea (PNG), Save the Children implements programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance, and livelihoods. Save the Children’s program portfolio includes education, including a project for solarization of selected schools in Bougainville.
Here your skills will be valued - Role Purpose
The REnew Pacific Project Manager, reporting to the Program Operations Director, will lead the planning, execution, and monitoring of a large-scale solarization initiative across schools in Bougainville. This role requires strong leadership, technical expertise in renewable energy, and the ability to coordinate with government agencies, contractors, and school administrations to ensure successful delivery of sustainable energy solutions. The REnew Pacific Project Manager ensures the technical support and oversight on all REnew project components. This will also include quality and timely delivery (within budget) of the project outcomes and contributing to staff-management, budget management and capability building of provincial and school-based staff in Bougainville. The manager will also be required to contribute to additional renewable energy programming as relevant.
Key Areas of Accountability
Project Management
Develop detailed project plans, timelines, and budgets for solar installations across multiple schools.
Ensure that REnew outcomes are effectively managed on time, within budget, and with quality, through direct management of the project team.
Ensure solar system designs meet safety, efficiency, and sustainability standards.
Ensure that REnew programming is in line with current global practices adapted to the local context and based on sound evidence.
Ensure all REnew programming meaningfully integrates principles of gender equality, disability and inclusion (GEDSI) at all levels, identifying and reducing barriers to access.
Ensure that all relevant Save the Children project method management (PMM) and mandatory tools are prepared, disseminated, and regularly updated as needed in line with project and/or external changes.
Ensure that all project teams fully understand the REnew project design, objectives, deliverables, and intended impact, outcomes and outputs.
Contribute to REnew technical and program briefs / communications as requested.
Budget and Financial Management
Serve as budget holder (as delegated) and budget manager.
Review and approve all financial transactions within delegated limits, ensuring the application of all financial and procurement policies and compliance standards.
Ensure that project budgets are properly forecasted and reviewed monthly; review transaction listings, monitor and address variances within Save the Children and donor requirements.
Assist in the preparation of budgets for new renewable energy projects as relevant and requested.
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) and Reporting:
Work with the MEAL team to ensure that projects have an updated log frame, MEAL workbook and data collection tools; ensure teams know how to use them.
Work with the MEAL team to ensure that program data is collated, analysed and used to assess project performance at all levels and to inform learning.
Co-organize regular review meetings and learning events that use project data to ensure learning is used to guide project implementation, design, and adaptation.
Lead on preparing donor reports and other official documentation in line with donor requirements and Save the Children quality standards.
Work with the MEAL team to ensure that all beneficiary feedback and accountability systems are functional, accessible, and used, including by children and marginalized groups.
Assist with research or assessments as required for development or humanitarian programming, in collaboration with internal and external teams.
External Relations; Stakeholder Management
Maintain strong relationships with government and non-government stakeholders in Bougainville. Liaise with education authorities, school leaders, and contractors to align objectives.
Represent Save the Children in key coordination mechanisms as relevant to the sector.
Team Management
Provide line management, mentoring, and coaching for the project teams.
Ensure that all team members have updated performance plans/reviews, and development plans based on identified capacity gaps. Facilitate regular 1-1 and (documented) team meetings.
Ensure that all team members understand and comply with all Save the Children, donor, and other applicable policies, principles, and procedures, including mandatory trainings.
Lead on recruiting new team members as relevant / appropriate. Ensure staff have completed all mandatory training and have up-to-date background checks.
Safeguarding Requirements
Maintain a child-safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, always acting in the best interests of children, as well as safeguarding all beneficiaries.
Comply with the Child Safeguarding Code of Conduct and child safeguarding and protection. policies and standards, as well as all other related policies, including reporting requirements.
Demonstrate the highest standards of behaviour towards children in private/professional life.
General
Fulfill other management duties (such as Extended Management Team Member) as required.
Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policies, procedures, work instructions and training, including all reporting requirements and processes.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Be aware of, document and manage the risks associated with the program activities, operations and workplaces, ensuring appropriate elimination or mitigation measures are applied.
Any other relevant duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Child Protection and Safeguarding Requirements
Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, always acting in the best interests of children.
Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s
Child Safeguarding Policy
,
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.
Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behaviour towards children in private and professional life.
Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being part of Save the Children’s family.
Maintain a safe and positive relationship when working with children and young people.
Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with Save the Children mandatory reporting processes.
Health, Safety, Security and Risk Management
Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training. Always act safely.
Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.
All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.
At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities. We value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.
Person Specification
It takes all types of people to do the challenging work we do. Here are some of the specific skills and experiences you’ll bring in this role:
Education Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Renewable Energy, Engineering, Project Management, or related field. Master’s degree is an advantage.
Required Skills, Abilities and Experience
At least eight (8) years of experience, with at least three (3) years in leadership positions.
Demonstrated experience delivering community-driven, renewable energy programming. Infrastructure management experience is an advantage.
Experience with a humanitarian or international non-governmental organisation is an advantage.
A solid understanding and mastery of program logic and the ability to ensure quality implementation of detailed activity plans on time and on budget.
Strong financial management skills and ability to use and analyse Excel-based financial reports.
Strong experience working constructively with government partners. Excellent communication/ influencing skills; ability to effectively converse with both technical and operational stakeholders.
Experience managing and building capabilities of diverse teams. Ability to work harmoniously in cross cultural environments.
Knowledge of the use of MEAL tools and data to produce reports and facilitate learning.
Demonstrated ability to think strategically, prioritize and meet deadlines in a complex and challenging environment. Strong work ethic and willing to take responsibility for his or her actions.
Solid computer skills including, but not limited to, Word, Excel, PowerPoint.
